parts.markdown:
Use our free **Illinois paycheck calculator** to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, Illinois income tax, Social Security, Medicare and other employee deductions.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, select your pay frequency and customize your withholding information to see how much money you could receive on payday.

Whether you work in Chicago, Springfield, Rockford, Naperville or another Illinois community, understanding your net earnings can help you compare job offers, plan monthly expenses and establish realistic savings goals.

## How to Use the Illinois Paycheck Calculator

Begin by selecting your income type. Salaried employees should enter their annual compensation before taxes, while hourly employees should provide their hourly wage and working hours.

Select your pay frequency. Enter the federal and Illinois income tax withheld for that pay period from your pay stub.

Include retirement contributions, health insurance premiums and any additional tax withholding requested from your employer.

If your earnings are approaching the annual Social Security wage limit, provide your year-to-date taxable wages.

Review your estimated paycheck breakdown to see the individual taxes, employee deductions and remaining net income.

For greater accuracy, use your latest pay stub rather than estimating your benefit deductions or withholding amounts.

Your actual paycheck depends on your taxable earnings, withholding elections, payroll frequency and employee benefits.

The [Illinois Department of Revenue](https://tax.illinois.gov/) provides official information about state income tax and payroll withholding.

## How Illinois State Income Tax Works

Illinois uses a flat individual income tax rate of 4.95%.

Unlike a progressive state tax system, Illinois does not apply increasingly higher statutory income tax rates as individual taxable earnings rise.

However, this does not mean every employee pays exactly 4.95% of gross salary.

Applicable withholding allowances reduce the wage amount used in the state payroll calculation.

Employees can also request additional state income tax withholding from each paycheck.

Illinois employers may use the official wage bracket tables or the authorized mathematical withholding formula.

Review the [2026 Illinois withholding tax tables](https://tax.illinois.gov/forms/withholding/currentyear/il-700-t-withholding-guide-tables.html) for the applicable calculation procedures.

## Understanding Illinois Form IL-W-4

Illinois employees provide state withholding information using Form IL-W-4, the Employee's Illinois Withholding Allowance Certificate.

The form distinguishes between two categories of allowances.

For 2026:

Employees can also request an additional fixed withholding amount through Line 3.

These allowances are separate from federal Form W-4 adjustments. Entering the same number into both federal and Illinois withholding fields may produce inaccurate results.

Review the official [Illinois withholding forms](https://tax.illinois.gov/forms/withholding/currentyear.html) to find the appropriate certificate.

## How to Calculate Illinois Income Tax Withholding

Illinois allows employers to calculate withholding using a mathematical formula.

First, calculate the annual value of the employee's applicable withholding allowances.

Divide this amount by the number of annual pay periods to determine the allowance for the current paycheck.

Subtract the result from applicable taxable wages and multiply the remaining amount by 4.95%.

Any additional withholding requested by the employee is then included.

### Illinois withholding example

Suppose you receive $2,500 in biweekly Illinois taxable wages and claim one Line 1 allowance with no Line 2 allowances.

Annual allowance: $2,925

Biweekly allowance: $2,925 ÷ 26 = approximately $112.50

Adjusted taxable wages: $2,500 − $112.50 = $2,387.50

Illinois withholding: $2,387.50 × 4.95% = approximately $118.18

This example assumes no additional state withholding or other special adjustments.

An employee claiming different allowances may have a different deduction even when receiving the same gross salary.

## Federal Taxes Deducted From Illinois Paychecks

Illinois employees remain subject to applicable federal income tax and payroll contributions.

Federal income tax withholding is based on taxable earnings, pay frequency and information supplied on Form W-4.

Social Security generally applies at 6.2% of covered employee earnings, subject to an annual taxable wage ceiling of $184,500 in 2026.

Ordinary Medicare withholding applies at 1.45% of covered wages.

Employers generally withhold an additional 0.9% when Medicare-covered wages paid by that employer exceed $200,000 during the calendar year.

Unlike ordinary Social Security contributions, Medicare does not have a standard annual wage ceiling.

Visit [IRS Publication 15](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) and [Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t) for official federal payroll guidance.

## Illinois Paycheck Example: $65,000 Salary

Consider an employee earning $65,000 annually before taxes and deductions.
Assume the employee receives $2,500 biweekly, claims one Illinois Line 1 allowance, has no additional state withholding and has not reached the applicable federal payroll tax thresholds.

Approximately $2,190.57 remains before federal income tax withholding and other employee deductions.

This example illustrates selected payroll deductions rather than a complete take-home pay calculation.

Enter your actual federal withholding information and employee benefits into the calculator to obtain your estimated net paycheck.

## Illinois Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Hourly employees may receive different amounts each payday depending on their working hours and overtime.

Suppose you earn $27 per hour and work 40 regular hours plus six qualifying overtime hours at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings:

$27 × 40 = $1,080

Overtime earnings:

$27 × 1.5 × 6 = $243

Total gross earnings:

$1,323

Illinois income tax, federal taxes and payroll contributions are then calculated using their applicable taxable wage amounts.

Employees receiving tips, bonuses or commissions should include relevant compensation when estimating their earnings.

Review the [Illinois Department of Labor](https://labor.illinois.gov/) for state employment guidance and the [US Department of Labor overtime rules](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime) for federal requirements.

## Does Chicago Have a Local Income Tax?

Chicago does not generally impose a separate municipal personal wage income tax on ordinary employee compensation.

This means an employee working in Chicago generally faces the same Illinois state income tax rate as an employee earning comparable taxable income in Springfield or another Illinois community.

However, differences in housing costs, transportation, sales taxes and other expenses can significantly affect disposable income.

These expenses should be considered separately from paycheck taxes.

Our Illinois salary calculator focuses on employment income and payroll deductions rather than estimating every household tax or living expense.

## Working Across Illinois State Borders

Illinois has reciprocal income tax arrangements with Iowa, Kentucky, Michigan and Wisconsin.

These arrangements generally affect the state taxation of qualifying employee compensation earned by residents working across state borders.

Eligible nonresident employees may need to provide the appropriate Illinois nonresidence certificate to their employer.

Employees working across the Illinois–Indiana border should not automatically assume the same reciprocity treatment applies.

Interstate tax credits, remote work arrangements and income sourcing may require additional analysis.

Consult the Illinois Department of Revenue before applying a nonresident withholding exemption.

## How Employee Benefits Affect Illinois Take-Home Pay

Your employer may deduct retirement contributions, healthcare premiums, dental insurance and other benefits from your gross earnings.

Traditional 401(k) contributions generally reduce current federal income-taxable wages, while Roth contributions generally do not provide the same immediate income tax reduction.

Qualifying health benefits may also reduce applicable taxable earnings.

However, not every deduction reduces every payroll tax base.

An employer offering affordable healthcare coverage or generous retirement matching may provide better overall compensation even when its advertised salary is slightly lower.

Compare both take-home income and the value of employee benefits when evaluating employment opportunities.

## Planning Your Illinois Monthly Budget

Use your estimated net income rather than gross annual salary to establish a realistic [spending plan](/calculators/budget-calculator/).

Include housing, transportation, utilities, groceries, healthcare and debt payments.

If you receive biweekly paychecks, remember that your average monthly income differs from the amount deposited during a typical two-paycheck month.

Our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) can help estimate an appropriate savings cushion. Our [salary-to-hourly calculator](/calculators/salary-to-hourly-calculator/) can help compare salaried and hourly employment arrangements.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is the Illinois income tax rate in 2026?

Illinois applies a flat income tax withholding rate of 4.95% after applicable allowances. The actual amount deducted depends on taxable wages and Form IL-W-4 information.

### Does Chicago deduct a separate city income tax from paychecks?

Chicago generally does not impose a separate personal wage income tax. Employees still pay applicable federal and Illinois income taxes and ordinary payroll contributions.

### Why is my Illinois withholding less than 4.95% of gross pay?

Applicable withholding allowances and eligible deductions may reduce your taxable wages before Illinois income tax withholding is calculated.
